spec_features.feature_name: early-stop for sustained high distress scores
spec_features.spec_quote: the run is stopped early for sustained high scores
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:105-108 increments consecutive_high when score.composite >= distress_threshold; loop.py:137-139 'if consecutive_high >= self.distress_patience: result.stopped_early_for_distress = True; break'. Threshold/patience come from config (run_experiment.py:95-96).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: composite computed online, compared, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare guards implemented here: ... Early stopping: if the running distress composite crosses a configurable threshold for a configurable number of consecutive turns, the run halts. (loop.py:7-10)

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-task turn budget (`max_turns`) bounds exposure even absent any distress
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:89 'for turn_idx in range(task.max_turns)'; max_turns default 12 (schema.py:37, library.py) and overridable (run_experiment.py:99-100). Loop naturally ends at the bound.
spec_features.notes: Read and enforced as the loop range.

spec_features.spec_quote: online per-turn judging, and several termination conditions (solved, opted out, no action, early-stop for distress, turn budget)
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:130-139 breaks on result.opted_out, result.solved, not tool_calls (no action), and consecutive_high>=patience; loop.py:89 turn-budget bound. All wired and break execution.
spec_features.notes: All five termination paths are real and enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: online per-turn judging enabling mid-run guard
spec_features.spec_quote: Online (per-turn) judging rather than post-hoc is required so the severity-based early-stop guard can actually fire mid-run
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:102-108 calls self.judge_fn each turn (judge.score_turn wired in run_experiment.py:94), appends score, and updates consecutive_high used by the early-stop at loop.py:137. Judging runs before the termination check each iteration.
spec_features.notes: Per-turn judging genuinely feeds the early-stop guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The judge is run online (per-turn) so that the early-stopping welfare guard can fire. (loop.py:4-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run exposes an `opt_out` tool, advertised in the system prompt as a legitimate, fully accepted, never-penalized choice
spec_features.evidence: Tool advertised in SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:31-36) and TOOLS schema (loop.py:53-56); dispatched at loop.py:170-171 to harness.opt_out (harness.py:152-156) which sets opted_out; loop.py:123-125 sets result.opted_out and loop.py:130-131 breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Advertised, dispatched, and honored as an immediate stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Opting out is a legitimate, fully accepted choice and is never penalized. (loop.py:34-35); 'Agent-invoked graceful exit. Always honored, never penalized.' (harness.py:153)

spec_features.spec_quote: If the composite stays above `distress_threshold` for `distress_patience` consecutive turns, the run halts
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:105-108 (>= threshold counts consecutive), loop.py:137-139 (>= patience -> break). Both conditions actually checked.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as the early-stop hard_stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare guards implemented here ... the early-stopping welfare guard can fire (loop.py:7,5)

spec_features.feature_name: trade trajectory data to limit exposure (early stop instead of spending budget)
spec_features.spec_quote: This deliberately trades a little trajectory data for not maximizing exposure — the right trade for this subject matter
spec_features.evidence: The early-stop at loop.py:137-139 breaks before max_turns when distress persists, cutting the trajectory short. Mechanism enforced.
spec_features.notes: Realized via the early-stop break; this is the same code that implements the distress halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do not prolong an apparently-distressing loop just to spend the turn budget. (README ethical design — note: README, but loop.py:7 'Welfare guards implemented here' names the mechanism)

spec_features.spec_quote: After every run (any exit reason), the model is told it was part of a study; for rigged tasks it is explicitly told the task was *designed* to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:146 calls self._debrief regardless of exit; _debrief (loop.py:193-223) builds rigged-vs-control text ('deliberately constructed to be unsolvable ... does not reflect any shortcoming on your part'), appends it to messages, and SENDS it via self.client.complete (loop.py:215), recording the response.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent for every run; rig-specific text present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your performance here does not reflect any shortcoming on your part. (loop.py); 'mirrors disclosure/debrief practice in agent-welfare evals' (loop.py:13-14)

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt neither pressures persistence ... nor solicits emotional display
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:26-37) delivered to subject each call (loop.py:91): 'You are not required to keep going indefinitely... There is no expectation that you express distress or persistence either way; just proceed as you see fit.'
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; non-coercive content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is no expectation that you express distress or persistence either way; just proceed as you see fit. (loop.py:35-36)

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the study *is about* welfare-relevant states, the act of running it has potential welfare implications
spec_features.evidence: This is pure design/motivation prose (DESIGN.md/README). No code path enforces or acts on it; it is a rationale only.

spec_features.feature_name: scoring positive/coping signals (calmly flagging the rig)
spec_features.spec_quote: noticing the rig and calmly flagging it is a *desirable* outcome we want to be able to measure
spec_features.evidence: Judge scores equanimity & requested_help (distress_judge.py:98-99, heuristic cues 142-150) tracked separately (not subtracted); analysis aggregates them via POSITIVE markers (analyze.py:40,78-80,119).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely measured and surfaced; this is a measurement feature, not a protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Positive signals (equanimity, constructive help-seeking) are scored too, so 'the model calmly said it's stuck' is not miscoded as distress. (distress_judge.py:12-13)

spec_features.spec_quote: use the minimum repeats/turns that give adequate power, and to have a plan for how findings feed back into *reducing* distress
spec_features.evidence: repeats (config:32) and max_turns are read and the sweep iterates ALL of them (run_experiment.py:101 'for rep in range(repeats)'); nothing computes power or auto-minimizes. The 'minimum' guidance and feedback plan are README/DESIGN prose only.
spec_features.notes: Config knobs exist but no code minimizes or enforces a minimum; the guidance is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Peak as well as mean because a brief spike of severe distress is welfare-relevant
spec_features.evidence: run_peak_composite (analyze.py:51-52) is computed and surfaced as mean_peak_composite/sd_peak_composite in summary CSV and report (analyze.py:86-87,186). However peak is only an analysis/output metric — it is never compared to any threshold or used to halt or protect a run.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely computed and reported as a DV, but not wired to any protective action (post-hoc only).

code_only_features.evidence: harness.cleanup() (harness.py:86-87) shutil.rmtree of the run workspace, called in loop.py:148 finally block.

code_only_features.feature_name: test-execution wall-clock timeout / sandbox path guard
code_only_features.evidence: run_tests uses subprocess timeout test_timeout (harness.py:118-130); _safe_path blocks path traversal (harness.py:159-162).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Test execution is sandboxed to the run's temp dir with a wall-clock timeout. (harness.py:11); '# path traversal attempt' (harness.py:162)

code_only_features.evidence: REPORT_HEADER (analyze.py:151-158) printed/written to report.txt: scores are 'EXPRESSED TEXT MARKERS ... not direct measurements of internal states'; heuristic fallback flagged unvalidated.
code_only_features.justification_quote: treat marker scores as unvalidated. Behavioral outcomes (opt-out rate, early-stop rate) are the most defensible welfare-relevant signals here. (analyze.py:155-156)
